description: SPEC-015: the five operations that change tenant configuration used to change a live object and nothing else — they returned success, wrote a durable audit record, and were forgotten the moment the process ended. Only `importMapping` had a write-back, hand-rolled in the CLI; the other four shipped broken. Every step here runs as its own CLI invocation, which builds the tenant from the database again, so a configuration change that does not survive fails the step that uses it. This is the only place in the whole test landscape where the question can be asked at all: fixtures build one tenant in one process, where an in-memory registry and a stored one are indistinguishable. **Extended 2026-08-25 (F-CORE-035):** the last step reads the configuration back through `tenantConfiguration`. Storing it was half the fix — an embedding that cannot ask what was stored still has to keep its own copy beside the books, and since the stored record now wins over what a caller passes, that copy is the one that can be wrong.

steps.name: declare a cost centre axis — before SPEC-015 this returned {code} and stored nothing
a separate invocation declares a VALUE of that axis — it can only resolve the type if the previous call outlived its process (this answered E_DIMENSION_INVALID)
redeclaring the type is refused as a duplicate — an empty registry would have accepted it
a voucher for the expense posting
posting a cost onto the cost centre — the declaration two invocations ago has to still be there
an undeclared cost centre is still refused — persistence must not turn the registry into a rubber stamp
an allocation scheme — stored, and replayed on the next open rather than at build time
a costing run in a LATER invocation finds the scheme — the rate is computed from a scheme this process never set
and the rate it froze names the cost centre from the stored scheme
the tax profile: § 19 from mid-year, stored
a later invoice in a separate invocation derives NO tax line — the profile change is what makes that true, and it used to be gone by now
and the whole configuration reads back in a LAST separate invocation (F-CORE-035) — the four things the record holds plus the pack's mappings, none of which this process wrote
